## One-Sentence Summary

A software tool that scans real-world tools with a phone or webcam, auto-generates precisely scaled outlines, and exports ready-to-make files so users can design and produce custom organizers without CAD skills.

## Problem

The creators argue that organizing tools and parts is slow and technical, typically requiring CAD expertise, manual measurements, or specialized hardware. This creates friction for makers and shops who want custom-fit inserts or boards tailored to their own tools.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product combines a mobile scanner and a desktop web app: users place a tool on paper, capture an image from about 3 ft (1 m), and the software scales and traces the outline to exact dimensions. The desktop app syncs scans, lets users refine contours, add labels, and preview inserts, then exports manufacturing-ready files for 3D printing, laser cutting, milling, or ordering through in-app partners.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Phone-based scanning with automatic scaling to true size.

-   Browser-based editor that syncs with mobile; instant updates across devices.

-   Exports: STL, SVG, DXF, and STP for printing, cutting, or routing; option to order directly in-app.

-   "New features" highlighted: faster interface; one-click STL export; peg-board design; custom drawer outlines; public library of tool shapes and inserts; search by name; webcam scanning; ability to purchase tools in-app.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Intended for makers and professional environments such as machine shops and commercial toolboard manufacturers---anyone needing quick, custom storage solutions for drawers, boards, or cases.

## Development Status

The campaign presents a working concept with both phone and desktop components and details of the forthcoming "new app," implying an active development phase focused on speed, features, and workflow polish.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

The team is "aiming to deliver the new app by January 1st." Stretch goals include a custom organizer library (noted as grid-style trays and bins) and a desktop installation for offline use. The team plans to ship the core first---catalog, search, drawer layouts, and DXF/SVG export---then add extras afterward.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds are described as directly enabling dedicated build time; if full-time staffing is not possible, senior contractors will be engaged, acknowledging that progress may be slower.

## Risks & Challenges

Stated risks include staffing and scope management, scanning accuracy variations due to lighting or finishes, file-format compatibility across machines, platform updates, and service uptime. Mitigations include shipping a focused core, calibration and manual edit tools, exporting standard formats, testing against OS/browser betas, using trusted cloud services with backups, and maintaining a status page.

## Team & Partnerships

The project is led by founders with mechanical engineering and sustainable additive manufacturing/product design experience. The campaign references in-app ordering through partners and a search for sustainable manufacturing partners.

## What's Included

Access to the software, the ability to scan and sync on mobile/desktop, editing and labeling tools, and exports in STL/SVG/DXF/STP; a public library of shapes and inserts is also described.

## Technical Details

-   Phone capture distance: \~3 ft (1 m).

-   Outputs: STL, SVG, DXF, STP.

-   Works via phone camera, webcam, and a browser-based desktop app; includes calibration and manual edits.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team plans hotfixes for platform changes, a status page for outages, and community features where users can browse shared projects and shapes. The campaign notes some source code may be updated using AI-generated code.

## One-Sentence Summary

A spring-loaded, trigger-actuated bottle opener that uses stored kinetic energy to eject caps cleanly while emphasizing durability and over-engineered craft.

## Problem

The creators frame traditional openers as simple prying tools that can feel mundane and imprecise, positioning a need for a more engaging, efficient, and precision-made alternative. They also highlight a desire for an object that blends utility with pride in workmanship---something that "reimagines" the act of opening a bottle into a satisfying, reliable motion backed by robust materials and construction.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product is a spring-loaded bottle opener that builds tension with a finger pull and releases via a trigger, ejecting the cap in a single, fluid motion. It is presented as an innovative tool inspired by professional gear, intended to merge form and function while standing out as a conversation piece and gift.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Spring-loaded mechanism that stores kinetic energy and releases with a trigger press.

-   "Clean" cap ejection claimed to occur in one motion.

-   Emphasis on long-lasting performance through durable materials.

-   Engineered with impact resistance in mind due to repeated contact from a spring-driven bolt.

-   Positioned as both functional tool and display-worthy object or gift.

## Target Users & Use Cases

The product is aimed at people who enjoy well-engineered gadgets and want an opener that is equal parts practical and conversation-starting. It is also pitched as a distinctive gift for enthusiasts who appreciate design-meets-utility objects.

## Development Status

The campaign introduces the tool as a new product emphasizing its engineered design and material choices; no testing data or certification results are presented on the page.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include: purchasing raw materials, investing in specialized machinery and custom molds, and bringing the manufacturing process in-house to support full-scale production. Specific milestone dates are not provided.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds are intended to:

-   Acquire aerospace-grade aluminum (6061), corrosion-resistant stainless steel, high-strength tool steel, and heat-treated springs.

-   Invest in equipment and custom tooling to internalize manufacturing.

-   Scale from a workshop concept to a full operational build.

## Risks & Challenges

The team cites potential delivery delays tied to broader supply-chain issues. They note having secured quotes and established partnerships to mitigate these risks and commit to transparent communication if unforeseen issues arise.

## Team & Partnerships

The founders describe inspiration drawn from a professional, emergency-services context and mention established partnerships (unnamed) supporting production planning and sourcing.

## Technical Details

Stated materials include aircraft/aerospace-grade aluminum (6061), corrosion-resistant stainless steel, high-strength tool steel, heat-treated springs, and impact-resistant TPU. The design is explicitly engineered for impact resistance and long-term reliability under repeated spring-bolt impacts. No dimensions, weight, or compatibility specs are listed.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises to communicate openly and transparently with backers throughout production, especially if unexpected issues occur.

## One-Sentence Summary

A compact, lightweight, precision milling machine that brings professional-grade machining accuracy and versatility to desktops for makers, students, engineers, and small teams.

## Problem

The creators argue that high-precision milling has been constrained to heavy, expensive industrial machines requiring dedicated workshops, leaving makers and learners with limited, underpowered, or imprecise desktop options. They frame this as a barrier to prototyping and education, asking why precision machining can't be both professional and portable.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product is presented as an ultra-compact, 2.4 kg milling machine delivering ±0.01 mm accuracy. It is positioned as "professional-grade" yet backpack-portable, intended to shift precision engineering from factory settings to everyday spaces such as homes, classrooms, labs, and offices.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Stepless spindle speed control from 0--10,000 rpm, with forward and reverse rotation for different materials (plastics, aluminum, wood, and more).

-   Professional-grade precision rated at ±0.01 mm. X, Y, and Z handwheels include graduated scales with 0.007 mm per division for fine adjustments.

-   Lightweight, durable build entirely from high-strength aluminum alloy; total weight 2.4 kg.

-   Compact footprint listed as 251 × 386 × 403 mm.

-   Changeable spindle chuck to switch quickly among cutting, engraving, and polishing tools.

-   Reduced vibration and noise for home and classroom use; described as energy-efficient.

-   Emphasis on simple, beginner-friendly operation with options for detailed control by advanced users.

-   Promoted as durable and consistently precise across repeated projects.

## Target Users & Use Cases

The page names makers and DIYers (custom parts, prototypes, jewelry), startups (rapid iteration without outsourcing), educators and students (hands-on precision engineering), and engineers (desktop or field use).

## Development Status

The team describes a progression from concept sketches to 3D CAD models, functional prototypes tested under real-world conditions, and small-batch validation to confirm durability, precision, and user experience before mass production.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Stated timeline: R&D kickoff (Feb 2024), Prototype v1 (Aug 2024), Prototype v2 and field testing (Dec 2024), final design freeze (Apr 2025), campaign launch (Sep 2025), pilot production run (Nov 2025), and mass production with delivery (Feb 2026).

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Support is framed as backing a movement to make professional tools portable, affordable, and widely accessible; backers are told they are supporting the broader vision as well as the product.

## Risks & Challenges

Acknowledged risks include component sourcing, assembly refinement, and logistics. As mitigation, the team cites its complete development process through prototypes and small-batch verification. The page asserts a commitment that every supporter will receive the machine as promised.

## Team & Partnerships

The founders describe a young, multidisciplinary team with backgrounds in mechanical engineering, industrial design, and electronics, motivated to make precision machining accessible beyond large factories. The page also shows third-party "featured on" mentions without further detail.

## What's Included

Add-ons listed include a 9-piece end-mill set and a 12-piece ER16 collet set. A "Packaging contents" section is referenced but not itemized on the visible page excerpt.

## Technical Details

-   Weight: 2.4 kg

-   Accuracy: ±0.01 mm

-   Handwheel resolution: 0.007 mm per division (X/Y/Z)

-   Spindle: 0--10,000 rpm; forward and reverse

-   Dimensions: 251 × 386 × 403 mm

-   Construction: high-strength aluminum alloy

-   Tooling: changeable spindle chuck (supports cutting/engraving/polishing)

-   Operational notes: reduced vibration/noise; described as energy-efficient and beginner-friendly.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The campaign emphasizes reliability through prior testing and states a guarantee of complete fulfillment of rewards.

## One-Sentence Summary

An online learning platform focused on human-centered AI education is evolving into an interactive, creator-driven ecosystem with a personal AI mentor, a hands-on agent playground, and tools for educators to publish micro-courses.

## Problem

The creators argue that AI is reshaping work faster than people can build the skills to keep up. They state that while technology changes daily, human learning lags behind, leaving individuals and teams without practical, up-to-date guidance on using AI effectively.

## Solution / Product Overview

The project expands an existing AI-learning platform into "2.0," positioning it as a social learning ecosystem that blends live AI news, scrollable micro-lessons, certification tracks, and interactive tools. The goal is to make AI learning accessible, simple, and guided by creators and a personal AI mentor.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   **AI Mentor:** A personalized guide that adapts to learner goals, recommends lessons, and supports practice of real-world skills.

-   **AI Agent Playground:** A space to experiment with automations (e.g., email summarization, invoice assistance, social media agents), with 10+ templates, tutorials, and progress tracking.

-   **Course Builder for Creators:** Tools for educators to build, publish, and monetize micro-courses, positioning the platform as creator-driven.

-   **Learning Content & Certifications:** Micro-courses, reels, and structured certifications (e.g., AI foundations and automation tracks) presented with stated durations and skills coverage.

-   **Enterprise Programs:** Mention of programs tailored to teams, including domain-specific learning (e.g., finance).

## Target Users & Use Cases

Individual learners seeking practical AI fluency; creators who want to teach and monetize AI courses; and professional teams pursuing strategic adoption of AI in functions such as marketing and finance.

## Development Status

The team says it has already built a foundation that includes live updates, micro-courses, and certifications. The campaign funds new "2.0" capabilities: AI Mentor and Agent Playground prototypes, expanded creator tools, and a global challenge.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

A four-phase timeline is provided: (1) AI Mentor prototype (February 2026), (2) AI Agent Playground launch (April 2026), (3) Creator Course Builder (June 2026), and (4) Global Challenge plus Certification 2.0 (September 2026).

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds support development of the Mentor and Playground prototypes, expansion of creator tools and certification, a first global fluency challenge, and design of a human-centered interface.

## Risks & Challenges

Identified risks include integrating secure, scalable AI systems, designing intuitive user experiences, and ensuring fairness and accessibility. Mitigations cited are partnering with experienced AI developers and educators, monthly updates, and offering early testing opportunities.

## Team & Partnerships

The project is presented as a global effort with contributors, interns, and partners. It notes collaboration with experienced AI developers and educators, and plans to work with responsible, ethics-minded providers.

## What's Included

Access to the platform's learning environment, including micro-courses, reels, certification tracks, the forthcoming AI Mentor, the Agent Playground with templates and tutorials, and creator tools for course publishing.

## Technical Details

Content is cloud-delivered; the team highlights use of cloud infrastructure powered by renewable energy, emphasis on digital certificates, and reusability of learning progress across career changes.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team commits to open communication, monthly updates, and opportunities for early testing. It also discloses use of AI in content creation with human review and reliance on licensed or open datasets.

## One-Sentence Summary

A donation app and website that connects people with vetted nonprofits, makes giving fast and secure, and provides clear updates showing the impact of each contribution.

## Problem

The creators say many people want to help but hesitate because it's hard to know which organizations are trustworthy, where the money goes, and whether it truly helps; the process often feels long and ends in unwanted emails and data sharing, which creates friction and reduces support for worthy causes.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product is a donation platform designed to reduce doubt and complexity. It connects users to a curated set of organizations that have been screened for transparency, accountability, and results, enables quick, secure donations, and delivers follow-up updates so donors can see how their generosity made a difference.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   **Vetted organizations:** Every listed nonprofit is reviewed for transparency, accountability, and proven outcomes.

-   **Smart discovery:** Tools help users find causes aligned with their values and interests.

-   **Simple, secure giving:** A streamlined flow aims to remove "endless forms" and confusing steps, enabling donations in under a minute.

-   **Real-time impact updates:** Donors receive updates from supported organizations to understand the effects of their gifts.

-   **Privacy protections:** The team commits to no spam, no data selling, and no pressure, limiting communications to gratitude and impact updates selected by the user.

-   **Transparent fees:** The platform states a flat 1% fee, with no hidden charges.

-   **Mobile and web access:** The experience is available via a mobile app and a web platform.

## Target Users & Use Cases

The product is pitched to both new donors and people who already give regularly. Primary scenarios include discovering trusted organizations (from large, global efforts to local, community causes), making quick donations with confidence, and staying connected through ongoing impact updates.

## Development Status

According to the page, the platform is built, nonprofits are already vetted, and the mission and product scope are defined; the creators present it as ready to expand to more users.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned work includes launching the web and mobile platform at scale, expanding outreach to additional nonprofits and prospective donors, and building tools that deliver more meaningful impact insights to users. Specific dates are not listed.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds are intended for launch activities, nonprofit and user outreach, and development of impact-insight tools that enhance donor feedback after giving.

## Risks & Challenges

The team identifies technical and operational challenges related to scaling for a broad user and cause base. They state prior startup and product-deployment experience, say the platform is built for flexibility and scalability, and commit to continued transparency as they grow.

## Team & Partnerships

The project is led by the founders, who cite experience leading people operations at a technology company that later went public, with a mission background in safety and impact. The platform features a mix of large international organizations and local community groups as partners, all described generically and subject to vetting.

## One-Sentence Summary

A computer-controlled macro rail slider and companion software that automate ultra-precise focus stacking and streamline macro image capture for consistent, high-quality results.

## Problem

The creators highlight how close-up work makes depth of field extremely shallow, so only a thin slice of a small subject (e.g., an insect or jewelry) appears sharp in a single shot. They also note frustrations with spending hours in post-processing, and with missed shots when exposure, ISO, or focus aren't correctly set before triggering via a simple shutter cable.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product moves a camera forward in ultra-precise increments to capture a sequence of images that can be focus-stacked into a fully sharp photograph. It integrates rail motion with camera control software to coordinate capture, download images instantly, and provide live view for accurate setup---reducing complexity while improving repeatability and accuracy.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Precision motion for smooth, accurate steps that deliver consistent stacking results; standard threaded mount points for quick tripod attachment.

-   Controller based on a straightforward state-machine design (no microcontroller), enabling instant power on/off and avoiding firmware update issues; upgrades occur in computer software.

-   Camera control software provides live view, setting adjustments, and direct capture/transfer for supported DSLR and mobile devices.

-   Open design with a full SDK, technical details, examples, and 100% free USB drivers to enable custom controllers and integration into diverse workflows.

-   Optional pairing with the company's turntables for one-click 360-degree spin macro photography.

-   Emphasis on durable, long-lasting construction using robust components.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Aimed at professional, hobbyist, and research photographers seeking reliable focus stacking. Illustrated use cases include tiny natural subjects and jewelry/product imagery, including 360-degree spin sequences.

## Development Status

A first prototype and working proof of concept are shown, including electronics testing, early rail assemblies, software screenshots, and sample results (e.g., stacked jewelry images and a 360-degree animation made with a prototype rail).

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Remaining work focuses on refining the SDK, performing final rail calibration, optimizing the already-completed camera control software to work seamlessly with the slider, and implementing a dedicated focus-stacking controller separate from the camera controller. The team projects first production units approximately four to six months after the campaign concludes.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

The campaign is positioned to transition the product from prototype to production and place the tool in the hands of creators, while completing software fine-tuning and integration steps noted above.

## Risks & Challenges

The team cites low technical risk due to a functioning prototype, with primary challenges in scaling manufacturing. Mitigations include prior product development and supply-chain experience and the limited remaining engineering scope (SDK refinement, calibration, and controller separation).

## Team & Partnerships

The team comprises technologists, hardware developers, photographers, and university professors with more than four decades of combined experience, including government-sponsored projects in geo-spatial imagery and urban terrain scanning.

## What's Included

Images of the shipping box show a slider, a controller, 24V-DC power supply, USB cable, motor cable, control cable, and protective foam packaging; signal and motor cables are separated to reduce interference.

## Technical Details

Diagrams indicate standard camera and tripod mounting points, non-slip feet for table use, controller LED status indicators, and travel bounds labeled at approximately 10 mm. The controller houses a PCB managing start/stop/forward/reverse states and drives a stepper motor.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The company will provide a complete SDK, open technical design details, and example integrations to support customization and ongoing workflow integration.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that lets shoppers scan product barcodes to see an animal-welfare "grade," then discover more humane and plant-based alternatives available in-store, nearby, or for delivery.

## Problem

The creators say shoppers are confused by numerous, often misleading, animal-welfare claims on product labels, leading to purchases that are cruel to animals, unhealthy, and harmful to the environment. They argue consumers currently lack tools to distinguish credible labels from "humanewashed" claims and cite external reporting on animal suffering, public-health impacts linked to intensive animal agriculture, and greenhouse-gas contributions from meat production.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product is a free barcode-scanning app that displays how humanely animals were raised for a given item via a simple grade. If a grade is unsatisfactory, the app surfaces plant-based and higher-welfare substitutes, including options found on the shelf, nearby, or via delivery. The scope spans groceries as well as cosmetics, accessories, pet food, and more.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Barcode scan returns an animal-welfare grade for animal-derived products.

-   Discovery tools to "see plant-based alternatives" and "find more humane options."

-   Store-specific browsing for alternatives available in-store, nearby, and for delivery.

-   "Take action" prompts, such as signing petitions or donating to nonprofits.

-   Future plans include: integration with a popular health-scoring app; personalized shopping lists by store based on preferences (e.g., welfare, price, distance); scanning an entire shelf/section to flag the most humane choices; optimizing online carts toward humane and plant-based picks; and a plant-based recipe library with submissions from well-known creators.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Everyday shoppers looking to align purchases with animal-welfare and health goals; people comparing on-shelf items quickly; online shoppers seeking humane substitutions; advocates wishing to make more humane purchasing habitual.

## Development Status

A working web prototype/database already catalogs higher-welfare animal products in the U.S., built from certifications the creators say meet the highest standards according to a third-party label guide. They report more than five thousand products across over fifty-five thousand locations and twelve thousand unique users to date, achieved without marketing.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Following the campaign's end in November, the team targets a beta release in January 2026 and a full launch in March 2026. Post-launch, the app will add the planned integrations, list-building, section-scanning, cart optimization, and recipe features noted above.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support marketing to drive awareness and adoption; development to convert the prototype into a mobile app with UI/UX and design enhancements; and user incentives (e.g., rewards for uploading receipts and completing surveys) to improve data quality.

## Risks & Challenges

The team identifies its main risk as achieving consumer awareness and adoption at scale. They note the product's broader impact depends on demonstrating sufficient demand to shift retailer and producer behavior. To support feasibility, they cite shopper-survey statistics on concern for animal welfare, common use of shopping apps, and health as a key purchase driver.

## Team & Partnerships

The project is led by a technologist with decades of software-engineering experience at major tech companies and a marketing lead with long-running campaign experience in media and advocacy. Advisors include leaders from multiple animal-welfare and food-systems organizations. The prototype received a grant from a philanthropic funder, fiscal sponsorship from a nonprofit, and data support from an animal-welfare organization.

## Technical Details

Product grades are derived from the stated standards of recognized animal-welfare and sustainability certification programs; higher standards receive higher grades.

## One-Sentence Summary

A hackable, open-source, Raspberry-Pi--based desktop device and software stack that lets developers build multimodal (voice, vision, IR, sensing) assistants and self-hosted apps with a simple GUI and language-agnostic API.

## Problem

The creators argue that building polished, interactive AI experiences on single-board computers is hard: self-hosting is fiddly, peripherals are fragmented, and most "home pods" are closed and difficult to customize for real deployments. They also note that remote access, headless setup, and long-term context/memory are recurring pain points.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product combines an extensible hardware unit (with microphones, speakers, display, keypad, sensors, IR, and camera) and an open software platform that supports dozens of AI providers plus local engines. A built-in GUI and Web UI enable setup, app installation via containers, system management, and remote development; a gRPC API lets any language call into multimodal UX functions.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Multimodal assistant: voice conversations with context retention and optional long-term memory via a configurable memory service.

-   Vision: on-device capture and image understanding; image generation by voice with results shown on the LCD.

-   Local or cloud AI: selectable STT/TTS/LLM/vision services and on-device engines; can point to a local model server.

-   Tool/MCP integration: function calling and MCP servers for custom knowledge and tasks (e.g., search, database queries, browser control).

-   System GUI (no keyboard/monitor): manage Docker apps, networking, users, SSH, remote access, resources, and filesystem.

-   IR control: omni-directional IR transmitter (4 LEDs) and wide-band receiver for universal-remote use cases.

-   Programmable UI & gRPC: add prompts/notifications and LED/audio UX from any language.

-   Extensibility: connectors for I2C sensors, swappable top module, and planned open HAT+ add-ons and PCB templates.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Aimed at developers, makers, and educators who want to prototype and deploy AI-enabled assistants, smart-home controls (including IR TV control), classroom projects, and self-hosted services (e.g., home automation, DNS filtering, remote networking).

## Development Status

The team states the core software is open-sourced; hardware and software have undergone EVT/DVT/PVT; a pilot run (100+ units) and beta testing have been completed. A browser-based emulator exists for trying UI/audio without full hardware.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Backers receive a partially assembled kit; initial shipments will draw from existing inventory, with mass production to follow campaign completion. Units for one board version ship first; finishes may be surveyed post-campaign. Ongoing software roadmap and discussions are maintained in public repos.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will be used to scale production, finalize documentation/tutorials, and potentially expand in-house assembly capability and manufacturing resiliency.

## Risks & Challenges

Identified risks include import tariffs, potential shipping delays at ports, and supply-chain uncertainty. Mitigations: pricing already accounts for tariff changes; exploring alternate manufacturing regions; capability to assemble certain PCBs in-house; and staged fulfillment from existing stock.

## Team & Partnerships

The founders emphasize multi-year software investment and open development; hardware accommodates common maker ecosystems and third-party add-ons; unnamed suppliers are engaged for manufacturing.

## What's Included

Partially assembled kit excluding the single-board computer; includes enclosure, logic boards, heatsink, power adapter, 32 GB microSD (pre-imaged), camera, speakers, ethernet cable, and screwdriver.

## Technical Details

1.54″ 240×240 TFT; 7-button silicone keypad; dual mics (48 kHz); stereo speakers (48 kHz, \<0.1% THD, 1 W/ch); line-out specs as listed; 27-LED ring; 5 MP camera included; supports specific official camera modules by board version; safe power button; IR receiver (20--60 kHz, \~5 m) and omni IR transmitter (940 nm, 4 emitters); temperature and ambient-light sensors; physical camera curtain and mic hardware switch; 32 GB microSD; active thermal management/overclocking support; dimensions 130×99×52 mm; weight \~340 g; compatible with two recent board generations.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises extensive "Getting Started" guides, tutorials, public discussions, example clients, and ongoing videos with product updates and demos, all aligned with an open-source release model.

## One-Sentence Summary

A bedside sleep companion that replaces the phone at night by combining audio content, sunrise alarms, private Bluetooth listening, and planned sleep insights into one app-free device for simpler, higher-quality rest.

## Problem

The creators argue that late-night phone use and decision fatigue undermine rest, citing scrolling, stress, and restless nights as common issues; an infographic highlights how many people sleep with their phones, how many adults report insufficient rest, and how minutes are lost nightly to "doomscrolling." They frame the core pain point as the difficulty of winding down and waking gently without bringing a smartphone to the bedside.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product is presented as a "true alternative" to mobile devices at night: a one-touch routine launcher with built-in calming audio, podcasts (via an over-the-air update), sunrise lighting, alarms, and---planned for a later software release---sleep insights that don't require wearables. The pitch emphasizes "no phones, no apps," and a design tuned for sleepy, in-the-dark use.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   One-touch bedtime routine with remembered preferences for content, volume, and light

-   Noise masking, nature-inspired soundscapes, and guided relaxations; regular new content

-   Full podcast player via OTA update

-   Flexible alarms, schedules, and Dynamic Sunrise using 120 LEDs with adjustable duration; can pair with progressive alarms

-   Bluetooth headphone streaming for private listening (A2DP, stereo), controlled by a tactile volume ring

-   50 mm full-range speaker with 360° diffused audio

-   Wi-Fi updates delivering ongoing improvements; no subscriptions

-   App-free experience and a comparison table claiming broader coverage of sleep needs than single-purpose devices

-   Certification from an external calm-technology program

-   General-wellness insights only; not a medical device

## Target Users & Use Cases

People who want phone-free nights; those sharing a room who need private listening through headphones; and anyone seeking calmer wake-ups with sunrise simulation and progressive alarms.

## Development Status

A first mass-production batch has been completed; the initial build is in transit to the U.S. The team expects initial shipping in mid-November with additional units in mid-December. Beta-tester testimonials are included.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Timeline shows: mass production (September 2025); campaign launch (October); begin shipping (November); complete backer shipments (December); OS v1.1 enabling podcasts (December 2025); OS 2.0 enabling sleep insights (March 2026).

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds support start-up, operations, and manufacturing; as a result, pledges are non-refundable and returns are not accepted.

## Risks & Challenges

Detailed risks and mitigations include: supply chain (materials secured for an initial multi-thousand-unit run; validated first run); certifications (completed for key regions); logistics (staggered shipments with buffers); product quality (in-line testing, burn-in, corrective action plans); software stability (staged, signed, rollback-capable updates); fulfillment (experienced partners, contingency carriers, warranty replacement). Ongoing production and logistics updates are promised.

## Team & Partnerships

A small team with backgrounds in robotics and consumer electronics leads the project; a certification body recognized for calm-technology principles validated the product.

## What's Included

The device, a 20 W USB-C power supply (US-style plug), a 1.5 m USB-C braided cable, and a quick-start guide. Default language is U.S. English, with more languages planned via software updates.

## Technical Details

Silent tactile controls and an ultra-dimmable, flicker-free touchscreen; directional, touch-adjustable lighting; Bluetooth A2DP headphone streaming; 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi for OTA updates and automatic time setting; sensors for ambient light, temperature, humidity, and contactless motion; microphone hardware present but disabled; setup requires no phone; dimensions 5.5 × 3.8 × 4.5 in; weight 2.3 lb. Privacy: no accounts, names, emails, ads, or subscriptions; on-device encrypted data; insights opt-in when launched.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

One-year limited warranty in eligible regions; responsive support; regular software/content updates via Wi-Fi; and periodic production/logistics updates during fulfillment.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that helps players find and organize quality pickup basketball games, track performance, and compete locally while building community.

## Problem

The creators describe how informal games become hard to sustain as people age and schedules fragment; coordinating through group texts fails, turnout is unreliable, and some alternatives lead to poor playing experiences. They frame this against broader social isolation, citing that many adults report loneliness and that regular sports participation correlates with meaningful reductions in loneliness and all-cause mortality. They also note that most adult athletes feel there's no effective solution for finding pickup games.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product is a single mobile hub that combines game discovery, logistics, and social performance tracking. It aims to replace ad-hoc texting with structured scheduling, make player quality and sportsmanship more transparent, and re-energize informal local basketball by making it easier to form reliable runs and communities.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Scheduling tools for organizing runs.

-   In-app analytics to "analyze your stats" and "track your wins."

-   Peer ratings with local leaderboards.

## One-Sentence Summary

## Problem
The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."
